sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
Interesting! When I moved the player to the right (col=50), the board configuration changed dramatically. The current image shows:
- Player at right side (col=50)
- Many green blocks visible (6 green blocks in a 2x3 grid on the left, and 3 green blocks in a row in the top area)
- Two blue regions (top and bottom)
- Black areas with gray dots
This is very different from when the player was at the left side (col=15). The board configuration depends on the player's position!
So the pattern is:
1. When player is at LEFT (col=15): one board configuration
2. When player is at RIGHT (col=50): another board configuration with green blocks
The green blocks appear when the player is at the right side. This suggests the goal might be:
- Move player to right side
- Click all green blocks
- Move player to left side (or some other position)
- Repeat until all areas are filled
Or maybe the goal is to click ALL green blocks that appear when the player is at the right side. Let me try clicking all the green blocks now.
Looking at the current image, I see:
- 3 green blocks in a row at the top (rows 15-17 area)
- 6 green blocks in a 2x3 grid on the left (rows 27-33 area)
- Total: 9 green blocks visible
Wait, let me count more carefully from the segmentation.

sections.label: TOOL CALL: python
sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
# Check current green blocks
seg = current_frame.segmentation
green = [n for n in seg['nodes'] if n['color'] == 'N']
pink = [n for n in seg['nodes'] if n['color'] == 'P']
blue = [n for n in seg['nodes'] if n['color'] == 'S']
player = [n for n in seg['nodes'] if n['color'] == 'b']

print(f"Green: {len(green)}, Pink: {len(pink)}, Blue: {len(blue)}, Player: {len(player)}")

# Get green block positions
for g in green:
    rows = [p[0] for p in g['boundary']]
    cols = [p[1] for p in g['boundary']]
    center_row = sum(rows) // len(rows)
    center_col = sum(cols) // len(cols)
    print(f"  Green at row={center_row}, col={center_col}, pixels={g['pixels']}")

# Click all green blocks
clicks = []
for g in green:
    rows = [p[0] for p in g['boundary']]
    cols = [p[1] for p in g['boundary']]
    center_row = sum(rows) // len(rows)
    center_col = sum(cols) // len(cols)
    clicks.append({'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': center_row, 'col': center_col})

action(clicks)
print(f"\nAfter clicking: level_completed={last_action_result.get('level_completed')}")

seg = current_frame.segmentation
green2 = [n for n in seg['nodes'] if n['color'] == 'N']
blue2 = [n for n in seg['nodes'] if n['color'] == 'S']
print(f"Green after: {len(green2)}, Blue after: {len(blue2)}")
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
